description: The field inventory of the DozerDB query log: one row per documented query log setting (settings), one row per documented query log field and per plain-text segment (fields), with where it appears (JSON key; plain segment, its position in %m order and the separator before it; detail levels; entry kinds), what it looks like (a value pattern), the example lines that show it, its compatibility status per release line with the reason, its format provenance and maintainer notes; and the shapes DozerDB defines where the manual is silent (shapes), each naming the rows it fixes and the example lines that show it. Positions -2 and -1 are the layout's timestamp and level, 0 the entry marker, 1 onwards the segments of %m; separator is the text between the previous present segment and this one; the segment's <name> placeholders are the names of the rows at that position (the plan and stack trace rows name theirs after the row). optional says whether the field may be absent from an entry of a kind and detail level it appears in: under a detail flag (queryParameters, queryPlan), when Neo4j tracked or reported a value (cpu, failureReason, errorInfo, stacktrace, transaction.failureReason) or when authentication is off (authenticatedUser); a plain segment that is absent takes its separator with it. A common row lists the kinds of both entry types (stacktrace: fail and rollback). The release-gate check composes the plain segments' patterns into one expression per entry shape, so a free-text pattern is lazy ((?s).*?), leaving the segments after it their text, and the stack trace's opens with the throwable's class name. Every example line is the %m of an entry exactly as PlainTextRenderer writes it from the record beside it (literal tabs, literal line breaks); its level is the Log4j level the layout adds and detailLevel the db.logs.query.enabled value it was written under; a shape's lines are literal lines for an entry no renderer produces (the fallback entry), pinned by the module's tests. A setting row carries its Neo4j default per line (null where the line's Neo4j does not declare it), whether it is dynamic, its status per line and notes; the module declares no setting of its own, so nothing is cross-checked against Java. Three readers share this file and so cannot disagree: the module's renderer tests (loaded from the classpath through query-log/pom.xml's test-resources mapping, so the one committed file is the one read), the release-gate check scripts/query-log-check.py and the docs generator scripts/query-log-docs.py. Statuses use the query log glossary's tiers; provenance uses the metrics glossary's values, pending for a field not yet emitted. The lines are the release lines: calendar (main, Neo4j 2026.x, Operations Manual 2026.10) and lts (lts/5.26, Neo4j 5.26.x, Operations Manual 5); a test derives the running line from the kernel version and the docs generator from distribution/config.json, so one file serves both branches. Reasons and shape texts are published on the compatibility page; notes never are.

calendar.description: main: Neo4j calendar versions (major 2026 and later)

settings.name: db.logs.query.enabled

calendar.reason: Read from Neo4j's own declaration, so the name, the default and the three values are Neo4j's. VERBOSE writes a start entry and an end entry for every query; INFO writes an end entry for every query whose elapsed time reaches db.logs.query.threshold and for every failed query; OFF writes nothing and costs one volatile read per monitor event. A change at runtime applies to the next query.

lts.reason: Read from Neo4j's own declaration, so the name, the default and the three values are Neo4j's. VERBOSE writes a start entry and an end entry for every query; INFO writes an end entry for every query whose elapsed time reaches db.logs.query.threshold and for every failed query; OFF writes nothing and costs one volatile read per monitor event. A change at runtime applies to the next query.

settings.notes: GraphDatabaseSettings.log_queries; the module declares no setting and reads this one through its ConfigurationAdapter with a Config listener, like the other ten.

settings.name: db.logs.query.threshold

calendar.reason: Compared with the query's elapsed time at INFO: a query at or above the threshold is logged, so the default 0s logs every query, sub-millisecond ones included. A failed query is logged whatever the threshold. Ignored at VERBOSE, as documented.

lts.reason: Compared with the query's elapsed time at INFO: a query at or above the threshold is logged, so the default 0s logs every query, sub-millisecond ones included. A failed query is logged whatever the threshold. Ignored at VERBOSE, as documented.

settings.notes: elapsedMillis >= threshold (strict greater-than would drop sub-millisecond queries under the default); the approach of Neo4j's last open source query logger (3.4), read for approach only.

settings.name: db.logs.query.transaction.enabled

calendar.reason: OFF by default, as in Neo4j, so enabling the query log alone adds no transaction entry. VERBOSE writes a start entry and an end entry for every transaction; INFO writes an end entry for every transaction open for at least db.logs.query.transaction.threshold and for every rollback caused by a failure. Every kernel transaction is a candidate, the system database's and Neo4j's internal ones included. The plain-text shape of a transaction entry is DozerDB's (see the shapes DozerDB defines).

lts.reason: OFF by default, as in Neo4j, so enabling the query log alone adds no transaction entry. VERBOSE writes a start entry and an end entry for every transaction; INFO writes an end entry for every transaction open for at least db.logs.query.transaction.threshold and for every rollback caused by a failure. Every kernel transaction is a candidate, the system database's and Neo4j's internal ones included. The plain-text shape of a transaction entry is DozerDB's (see the shapes DozerDB defines).

settings.notes: LoggingPolicy.forTransactions over the open time measured at commit or rollback; no filter by origin, because an audit record that filtered would have to explain each omission.

settings.name: db.logs.query.transaction.threshold

calendar.reason: Compared with how long the transaction had been open, measured at its commit or rollback, at INFO; a rollback caused by a failure is logged whatever the threshold. Ignored at VERBOSE.

lts.reason: Compared with how long the transaction had been open, measured at its commit or rollback, at INFO; a rollback caused by a failure is logged whatever the threshold. Ignored at VERBOSE.

settings.notes: Open time = nanoTime - KernelTransaction.startTimeNanos() in whole milliseconds; the kernel exposes no end time for a rollback.

settings.name: db.logs.query.parameter_logging_enabled

calendar.reason: false leaves the parameters out of the entry: the plain segment goes with its separator and the JSON key is absent, never an empty {}.

lts.reason: false leaves the parameters out of the entry: the plain segment goes with its separator and the JSON key is absent, never an empty {}.

settings.notes: The record's parameters are null; the renderers drop a null field. The dropped segment is end-verbose-parameters-off.

settings.name: db.logs.query.max_parameter_length

calendar.reason: Applied to each parameter value, as the manual says: a value longer than the maximum is cut to that many characters and ... is appended inside the value, a string keeping its closing quote, so the entry still reads as a Cypher map.

lts.reason: Applied to each parameter value, as the manual says: a value longer than the maximum is cut to that many characters and ... is appended inside the value, a string keeping its closing quote, so the entry still reads as a Cypher map.

settings.notes: ParameterMaps prints each value with its own budget; PrettyPrinter's own budget is not used (it drops the closing quote and brace and writes no ellipsis on a chunk boundary). The cut is end-verbose-parameters.

settings.name: db.logs.query.obfuscate_literals

calendar.reason: Neo4j's own obfuscation of the query text: Community computes the obfuscated text once per compiled query and caches it with the query, so a change reaches a cached query after CALL db.clearQueryCaches(), as documented; passwords are masked at every setting, and a query that cannot be parsed has its text withheld, as the manual says. Parameter values are not obfuscated by this setting: they are written as they are, except that a password parameter is masked at every setting; to keep parameter values out of the log set db.logs.query.parameter_logging_enabled=false.

lts.reason: Neo4j's own obfuscation of the query text: Community computes the obfuscated text once per compiled query and caches it with the query, so a change reaches a cached query after CALL db.clearQueryCaches(), as documented; passwords are masked at every setting, and a query that cannot be parsed has its text withheld, as the manual says. Parameter values are not obfuscated by this setting: they are written as they are, except that a password parameter is masked at every setting; to keep parameter values out of the log set db.logs.query.parameter_logging_enabled=false.

settings.notes: QuerySnapshot.obfuscatedQueryText() and obfuscatedQueryParameters(). On the routed Bolt and HTTP path at Neo4j 2026.10 the change already applies to the next query; the cache-clear rule is exact for embedded and cached queries (ParametersAndObfuscationIT).

settings.name: db.logs.query.obfuscate_errors

calendar.reason: The failure reason of a failed-query entry and every statusDescription of its errorInfo become Neo4j's obfuscated status description, and no stack trace follows the entry, in both layouts.

lts.reason: Neo4j 5.26 has no obfuscated status description, so the standard description of the GQLSTATUS code (condition and sub-condition, without the message) stands in for the failure reason and at every level of errorInfo; no stack trace follows the entry, as on the calendar line.

settings.notes: ObfuscatedErrorDescriptions.of(status): ErrorGqlStatusObject.obfuscatedStatusDescription(), falling back to the standard description of the code; the LTS port deletes the first line only. The example is fail-verbose-obfuscated-errors.

settings.name: db.logs.query.plan_description_enabled

calendar.reason: Attaches Neo4j's own EXPLAIN rendering of the plan to the end entry: on the lines after the plain line, and as the one JSON string queryPlan. A start entry never carries a plan and a query that failed to compile has none. The placement is DozerDB's (see the shapes DozerDB defines).

lts.reason: Attaches Neo4j's own EXPLAIN rendering of the plan to the end entry: on the lines after the plain line, and as the one JSON string queryPlan. A start entry never carries a plan and a query that failed to compile has none. The placement is DozerDB's (see the shapes DozerDB defines).

settings.notes: QueryPlans.tableOf reads queryPlanSupplier().get().toString() on the ending thread only when the setting is on; no neo4j-cypher dependency, so the LTS line shares the code. The example is end-verbose-plan.

settings.name: db.logs.query.early_raw_logging_enabled

calendar.reason: Moves the start entry to the moment the query is received, before parsing and obfuscation, so a query that hangs or fails in parsing is still recorded, with its raw text and parameters (a password literal in clear, as the manual says of the setting); the end entry of the same query follows the obfuscation settings as always, and db.logs.query.parameter_logging_enabled and db.logs.query.max_parameter_length still apply. The early start entry's shape is DozerDB's (see the shapes DozerDB defines).

lts.reason: Moves the start entry to the moment the query is received, before parsing and obfuscation, so a query that hangs or fails in parsing is still recorded, with its raw text and parameters (a password literal in clear, as the manual says of the setting); the end entry of the same query follows the obfuscation settings as always, and db.logs.query.parameter_logging_enabled and db.logs.query.max_parameter_length still apply. The early start entry's shape is DozerDB's (see the shapes DozerDB defines).

settings.notes: LoggingPolicy.writesStartEntry(StartEvent): RECEIVED (startProcessing, the only event before the obfuscator; on the upstream watchlist as Fragile) under the setting, PARSED (startExecution) otherwise; exactly one start entry per query either way. The example is start-verbose-early.

settings.name: db.logs.query.annotation_data_format

calendar.reason: Applies to the JSON layout only, as documented: CYPHER writes the annotation data as the Cypher-map string, JSON as an object, FLAT_JSON as an object whose nested maps are folded into dotted keys; keys are sorted in every format, and the plain line is always the Cypher map. JSON is the default of this line; Neo4j 5.26 defaults to CYPHER.

lts.reason: Applies to the JSON layout only, as documented: CYPHER writes the annotation data as the Cypher-map string, JSON as an object, FLAT_JSON as an object whose nested maps are folded into dotted keys; keys are sorted in every format, and the plain line is always the Cypher map. CYPHER is the default of this line; Neo4j 2026 defaults to JSON.

settings.notes: AnnotationDataFormat {CYPHER, JSON, FLAT_JSON} in the module's own words; FieldMapRenderer.render(entry, format). The default differs per line in GraphDatabaseSettings (JSON at 2026.10.1, CYPHER at 5.26.32).

settings.name: db.logs.query.annotation_data_as_json_enabled

calendar.reason: Not read. Neo4j removed the setting in the 2026 line and no longer declares it, so Neo4j's own configuration handling decides what a neo4j.conf that still sets it does; use db.logs.query.annotation_data_format, which replaced it.

lts.reason: Not read, although Neo4j 5.26 still declares it (deprecated since 5.12): a neo4j.conf that sets it starts and the value changes nothing; use db.logs.query.annotation_data_format, which replaced it.

settings.notes: The one Unsupported row of the matrix: dropped on both lines because its replacement exists on both. Declared at 5.26.32 as log_queries_annotation_data_as_json (dynamic); absent at 2026.10.1. The module reads neither it nor any internal.dbms.logs.query.* key.

fields.name: time

calendar.reason: Written by Neo4j's layout: the shipped pattern %d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSSZ}{GMT+0} in plain text, the timestamp resolver in JSON.

lts.reason: Written by Neo4j's layout: the shipped pattern %d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSSZ}{GMT+0} in plain text, the timestamp resolver in JSON.

fields.notes: Not a field of the record; QueryLogFile recognises an entry by it. Positions -2 and -1 are the layout's two prefixes before %m.

fields.name: level

calendar.reason: Written by Neo4j's layout (%-5p, so INFO is followed by two spaces) from the InternalLog method the entry is written with: INFO for start and success entries, ERROR for a failed-query entry, for a rollback caused by a failure and for a fallback entry.

lts.reason: Written by Neo4j's layout (%-5p, so INFO is followed by two spaces) from the InternalLog method the entry is written with: INFO for start and success entries, ERROR for a failed-query entry, for a rollback caused by a failure and for a fallback entry.

fields.notes: The manual shows INFO only; ERROR for failures is DozerDB's choice, recorded on the failureReason row and, for transactions, on the transaction.failureReason row.

fields.name: type

calendar.reason: The constant the message puts in the field map: query for query entries, transaction for transaction entries.

lts.reason: The constant the message puts in the field map: query for query entries, transaction for transaction entries.

fields.notes: JSON only, the manual's type field: query on every query entry's field map, transaction on a transaction entry's. Never in the plain line.

fields.name: stacktrace

calendar.reason: Present when the entry carries a throwable, as the manual says: Log4j writes it on the lines after the plain line and as the JSON stacktrace field. DozerDB hands Neo4j's exception to Log4j for every failed-query entry, none under obfuscate_errors, and for every rollback Neo4j reports with a throwable.

lts.reason: Present when the entry carries a throwable, as the manual says: Log4j writes it on the lines after the plain line and as the JSON stacktrace field. DozerDB hands Neo4j's exception to Log4j for every failed-query entry, none under obfuscate_errors, and for every rollback Neo4j reports with a throwable.

fields.notes: Both layouts: QueryLogWriter.error with the cause, which Log4j writes after the plain line and as the JSON stacktrace field (the layout's exception resolver, cut at the first line break with the layout's suffix). The four-argument endFailure carries no throwable, but Cypher passes the exception itself as the GQL status object, which the adapter uses as the cause. Under obfuscate_errors the throwable is dropped, so no trace follows (fail-verbose-obfuscated-errors). A common row names the kinds of both entry types: fail for a failed-query entry, rollback for a rollback Neo4j reported with a throwable (transaction-rollback-failure-bolt).

fields.name: event

calendar.reason: The manual's only start entry is a Neo4j 4.4 capture; a 2026 start entry is DozerDB's shape: the end grammar with zeroed values behind the documented 'Query started: ' prefix; under early_raw_logging_enabled the early start entry carries transaction id:0 and the database <none>. Success and failed-query entries carry no plain marker; JSON names the event.

lts.reason: The manual's only start entry is a Neo4j 4.4 capture; a Neo4j 5 start entry is DozerDB's shape: the end grammar with zeroed values behind the documented 'Query started: ' prefix; under early_raw_logging_enabled the early start entry carries transaction id:0 and the database <none>. Success and failed-query entries carry no plain marker; JSON names the event.

fields.notes: Written from Neo4j's startExecution event, which fires once the query is parsed and obfuscated, so a query that fails to compile has no start entry; under db.logs.query.early_raw_logging_enabled it is written instead from startProcessing, when the query is received, so such a query keeps its start entry (start-verbose-early). Exactly one start entry per query either way: the policy picks the event from the configuration each event carried. In JSON the key is event with start, success or fail.

fields.name: id

calendar.reason: The query id (ExecutingQuery.internalQueryId(), incremental from 1 per server start), written at VERBOSE only on both lines, as the manual's JSON field list says; the manual's plain-text field list calls the prefix a connection id and shows it under a stated INFO configuration, which DozerDB does not follow.

lts.reason: The query id (ExecutingQuery.internalQueryId(), incremental from 1 per server start), written at VERBOSE only on both lines, as the manual's JSON field list says; the manual's plain-text field list calls the prefix a connection id and shows it under a stated INFO configuration, which DozerDB does not follow.

fields.notes: The current manual's plain-text list calls id: a connection id and shows it under a stated INFO configuration; the design settled on the query id at VERBOSE, the one number both layouts can share. The example is end-verbose-bolt-manual.

fields.name: transactionId

calendar.reason: The outer transaction's sequence number, the number SHOW TRANSACTIONS exposes; -1 for a query that failed before it was bound to a transaction.

lts.reason: The outer transaction's sequence number, the number SHOW TRANSACTIONS exposes; -1 for a query that failed before it was bound to a transaction.

fields.notes: QuerySnapshot.transactionSequenceNumber(). KernelTransaction.getTransactionId() exists only after commit and is not this number. An early start entry (early_raw_logging_enabled) is written before the query has reached a transaction and carries 0 on every path, so a reader can tell it from a start entry written after planning; -1 is Neo4j's own value on a query that ended without ever being bound (fail-verbose-no-database).

fields.name: elapsedTimeMs

calendar.reason: Wall time from the query's start, microseconds truncated to milliseconds; 0 on a start entry.

lts.reason: Wall time from the query's start, microseconds truncated to milliseconds; 0 on a start entry.

fields.notes: The separator after this segment is ': ' (colon, space), not ' - '.

fields.name: planning

calendar.reason: Compilation time in milliseconds, always present (the 4.4 toggle is gone); 0 on a start entry.

lts.reason: Compilation time in milliseconds, always present (the 4.4 toggle is gone); 0 on a start entry.

fields.notes: Shares one parenthesised segment with waiting. The 4.x cpu: value is not in this parenthesis: db.track_query_cpu_time says the time is 'not in the query.log'.

fields.name: cpu

calendar.reason: JSON only, and only when db.track_query_cpu_time=true: Neo4j's snapshot has no CPU figure otherwise, and DozerDB never invents one. Never in the plain line.

lts.reason: JSON only, and only when db.track_query_cpu_time=true: Neo4j's snapshot has no CPU figure otherwise, and DozerDB never invents one. Never in the plain line.

fields.notes: QuerySnapshot.cpuTimeMicros() is empty under the default db.track_query_cpu_time=false; the record carries cpuMillis as null then and the key is absent. With the setting on (it is dynamic) the next end entry carries it. The example's line shows that the plain text is unchanged.

fields.name: waiting

calendar.reason: Time spent waiting on locks or other queries, in milliseconds; 0 on a start entry.

lts.reason: Time spent waiting on locks or other queries, in milliseconds; 0 on a start entry.

fields.notes: Shares the parenthesised segment with planning.

fields.name: allocatedBytes

calendar.reason: The heap high-water mark of the query; 0 on a start entry.

lts.reason: The heap high-water mark of the query; 0 on a start entry.

fields.notes: Neo4j reports -1 (allocations not tracked) after a retry; written as it comes.

fields.name: pageHits

calendar.reason: Page cache hits of the query's transactions; 0 on a start entry.

lts.reason: Page cache hits of the query's transactions; 0 on a start entry.

fields.notes: Shares one segment with pageFaults.

fields.name: pageFaults

calendar.reason: Page cache faults of the query's transactions; 0 on a start entry.

lts.reason: Page cache faults of the query's transactions; 0 on a start entry.

fields.notes: Shares one segment with pageHits.

fields.name: source

calendar.reason: Community's ClientConnectionInfo.asConnectionDetails(): the Bolt shape is the manual's; the HTTP shape of the transactional endpoint (server-session, scheme, client host, request path) and the embedded shape (embedded-session plus its own tab) are shown by no 4.x+ manual example. A query over the Query API, which Neo4j 2026 serves over an in-process Bolt channel, carries the Bolt shape with neo4j-query-api/v2 as the client and local channel addresses.

lts.reason: Community's ClientConnectionInfo.asConnectionDetails(): the Bolt shape is the manual's; the HTTP shape of the transactional endpoint (server-session, scheme, client host, request path) and the embedded shape (embedded-session plus its own tab) are shown by no 4.x+ manual example. A query over the Query API, which Neo4j serves over an in-process Bolt channel, carries the Bolt shape with neo4j-query-api/v2 as the client and local channel addresses.

fields.notes: asConnectionDetails() is deprecated upstream (watchlist, Fragile). The segment's tabs are literal; the manual's HTML expands them to spaces.

fields.name: database

calendar.reason: The database name after one tab, as documented; <none> for a query that was never bound to a database, which the manual documents for JSON only and DozerDB writes in the plain line too.

lts.reason: The database name after one tab, as documented; <none> for a query that was never bound to a database, which the manual documents for JSON only and DozerDB writes in the plain line too.

fields.notes: QuerySnapshot.databaseId() is empty until the query is bound; the <none> string is not in Community. An early start entry (early_raw_logging_enabled) carries <none> on every path, the routed query not yet being routed and the shape being one; the end entry carries the database.

fields.name: executingUser

calendar.reason: The executing user, the plain line's one username ('Username of the query executioner'); empty when authentication is disabled.

lts.reason: The executing user, the plain line's one username ('Username of the query executioner'); empty when authentication is disabled.

fields.notes: Impersonation is visible in JSON only, where authenticatedUser sits beside it.

fields.name: authenticatedUser

calendar.reason: JSON only, as the manual lists it: the authenticated user beside executingUser, so impersonation is visible in JSON; the plain line shows the executing user alone and never the authenticated one.

lts.reason: JSON only, as the manual lists it: the authenticated user beside executingUser, so impersonation is visible in JSON; the plain line shows the executing user alone and never the authenticated one.

fields.notes: QuerySnapshot.authenticatedUsername(), present on every entry whose snapshot names one, as the manual lists it unconditionally; impersonation shows as a differing executingUser beside it. Absent, like every null field, when authentication is off and Neo4j reports no name.

fields.name: query

calendar.reason: The query text verbatim, its own line breaks included, obfuscated per db.logs.query.obfuscate_literals with passwords always masked; withheld under obfuscate_literals for a query that cannot be parsed, as the manual says.

lts.reason: The query text verbatim, its own line breaks included, obfuscated per db.logs.query.obfuscate_literals with passwords always masked; withheld under obfuscate_literals for a query that cannot be parsed, as the manual says.

fields.notes: The obfuscated text is what the entry shows, except on the early start entry of db.logs.query.early_raw_logging_enabled, which is written when the query is received, before parsing, from the raw text, so a query that fails or hangs in parsing is recorded, a literal stays under obfuscate_literals and a password literal is in clear, as the manual says of the setting; the end entry of the same query follows the rules below (start-verbose-early, EarlyRawLoggingIT). Otherwise: Community computes it once per compiled query and caches it with it, masking passwords, sensitive procedure arguments and credential URLs at every setting and every literal under obfuscate_literals (a user-management statement's user name is a literal too). The raw text stands in for a query that failed before its obfuscator existed (a parse or semantic error), so the record stays complete, except under obfuscate_literals, when the text is withheld as the manual says for a query that cannot be parsed: the segment is empty and the JSON key absent. A changed obfuscate_literals reaches a cached embedded query after CALL db.clearQueryCaches() and the next routed (Bolt, HTTP) query at once on Neo4j 2026.10, which picks the view with the live setting (ParametersAndObfuscationIT).

fields.name: queryParameters

calendar.reason: The parameters as Neo4j's PrettyPrinter single-line Cypher map ({} when there are none); db.logs.query.max_parameter_length truncates each value with ... inside the value, and parameter_logging_enabled=false drops the segment rather than writing {}. The manual shows {} only.

lts.reason: The parameters as Neo4j's PrettyPrinter single-line Cypher map ({} when there are none); db.logs.query.max_parameter_length truncates each value with ... inside the value, and parameter_logging_enabled=false drops the segment rather than writing {}. The manual shows {} only.

fields.notes: Rendering is Community's PrettyPrinter with the single quote mark and entities by reference, each value printed with its own budget (adapter ParameterMaps): max_parameter_length cuts a value to that many characters and appends ... inside the value, a string keeping its closing quote and a list or map cut in its text, so the entry still reads as a map. Parameters are never literal-obfuscated (the manual points to parameter_logging_enabled for that); a password parameter is ****** at every setting, except on the early start entry of early_raw_logging_enabled, which shows the raw map; parameter_logging_enabled and max_parameter_length apply to it all the same, since they are not obfuscation. end-verbose-parameters is the cut at a maximum of 10, end-verbose-parameters-off the dropped segment.

fields.name: runtime

calendar.reason: Community's lower-case runtime name, or null when the query never reached a runtime: on every start entry (as the manual shows) and on a query that failed before compilation.

lts.reason: Community's lower-case runtime name, or null when the query never reached a runtime: on every start entry (as the manual shows) and on a query that failed before compilation.

fields.notes: The manual shows pipelined and null; slotted and interpreted come from the same accessor. null on an early start entry too (start-verbose-early). Optional for the JSON layout: a start entry has no runtime yet and the key is absent, where the plain line writes runtime=null.

fields.name: annotationData

calendar.reason: The transaction's metadata (tx.setMetaData) as a Cypher map with unquoted keys and single-quoted strings in the plain line regardless of db.logs.query.annotation_data_format, which the manual says affects JSON only; keys sorted, since the manual's examples fix no order.

lts.reason: The transaction's metadata (tx.setMetaData) as a Cypher map with unquoted keys and single-quoted strings in the plain line regardless of db.logs.query.annotation_data_format, which the manual says affects JSON only; keys sorted, since the manual's examples fix no order.

fields.notes: A null metadata value renders as <null> in the Cypher map. In JSON, db.logs.query.annotation_data_format selects the same Cypher-map string (CYPHER), a JSON object (JSON, the calendar line's default) or an object whose nested maps are folded into dotted top-level keys (FLAT_JSON); keys sorted in every format. Neo4j 5.26's default is CYPHER.

fields.name: failureReason

calendar.reason: The failed-query entry is DozerDB's shape: level ERROR, the success grammar plus ' - <failure reason>' last and the stack trace after; the manual documents no failed query line. Written whatever the threshold. The JSON field is deprecated upstream and kept beside errorInfo because parsers key on it.

lts.reason: The failed-query entry is DozerDB's shape: level ERROR, the success grammar plus ' - <failure reason>' last and the stack trace after; the manual documents no failed query line. Written whatever the threshold. The JSON field is deprecated upstream and kept beside errorInfo because parsers key on it.

fields.notes: Neo4j's message may span lines (a syntax error adds the query and a caret). Absent when Neo4j reports a null reason: the entry then ends with the annotations. Under obfuscate_errors the obfuscated status description replaces the message (fail-verbose-obfuscated-errors), and a failure without a status object carries no reason, since nothing safe could stand in.

fields.name: errorInfo

calendar.reason: JSON only: the GQLSTATUS tree (GQLSTATUS, statusDescription, classification, position, nested cause) from the ErrorGqlStatusObject Neo4j reports; absent when the failure carries none.

lts.reason: JSON only, as on the calendar line, with Neo4j 5.26's GQLSTATUS tree: an error Neo4j 5.26 raises without a GQL status of its own (a variable not defined, for instance, which the router reports before the query reaches a database) carries the default 50N42 with no position and no cause, where the manual's example shows 42N62 with a position; an error with a GQL status carries its tree and position as on the calendar line. obfuscatedStatusDescription() does not exist at 5.26, so under obfuscate_errors the standard description of the GQLSTATUS code (condition and sub-condition, no message) stands in at every level of the tree.

fields.notes: Object-valued, so no pattern. Built in the adapter from the ErrorGqlStatusObject Neo4j reports (gqlStatus, statusDescription, getClassification unless UNKNOWN, the diagnostic record's _position as column/offset/line, cause() recursively); the record carries it as plain maps and strings. fail-verbose-bolt's tree is the manual's example. Under obfuscate_errors every level's statusDescription is the obfuscated one, parameters Neo4j lists as non-sensitive (a variable name) kept (fail-verbose-obfuscated-errors).

fields.name: queryPlan

calendar.reason: Only under db.logs.query.plan_description_enabled: the text of the ExecutionPlanDescription (Neo4j's EXPLAIN rendering: header lines, the operator table, the summary) on the lines after the entry in plain text and one string with embedded line breaks in JSON; the manual documents the field's presence and names the table, but fixes neither the placement nor the JSON type.

lts.reason: Only under db.logs.query.plan_description_enabled: the text of the ExecutionPlanDescription (Neo4j's EXPLAIN rendering: header lines, the operator table, the summary) on the lines after the entry in plain text and one string with embedded line breaks in JSON; the manual documents the field's presence and names the table, but fixes neither the placement nor the JSON type.

fields.notes: Only when db.logs.query.plan_description_enabled is true (Compatible: Neo4j's name, default false, dynamic; its row is in the settings array). The text is Community's own rendering of the ExecutionPlanDescription the snapshot's queryPlanSupplier() hands out (toString(): the Cypher version, planner and runtime header lines each followed by a blank line, the tree table with one row per operator and the columns that have a value, Operator | Id | Details | Estimated Rows for a plain execution, then 'Total database accesses: ?'), read on the ending thread, so the same code serves both lines and DozerDB draws nothing itself. The supplier is set once the outermost query has compiled and is never cleared, so a query that failed while running has its table and a query that failed to compile, a composite parent query or a mid-retry failure has none, whatever the setting. Always the EXPLAIN shape, also for PROFILE: no Rows, DB Hits, Page Cache Hits/Misses or Time (ms) column can appear, because the description is derived from the logical plan and never from the result. Line breaks are the platform's, as the layout's own are; the JSON layout escapes them, so the entry stays one object per line, cut like every other string at the layout's maxStringLength (16 KiB by default, 32 KiB with Neo4j's shipped neo4j.conf). A start entry never carries a plan.

fields.name: executionPlanCacheKeyHash

calendar.reason: JSON only: the plan cache key hash as eight upper-case hex digits, 00000000 for a start entry, as documented.

lts.reason: JSON only: the plan cache key hash as eight upper-case hex digits, 00000000 for a start entry, as documented.

fields.notes: String.format("%08X", QuerySnapshot.executionPlanCacheKeyHash()); 00000000 on a start entry because the adapter does not read the hash before planning, the early start entry included.

fields.name: queryLang

calendar.reason: JSON only: CYPHER 5 or CYPHER 25 from the snapshot's Cypher version.

lts.reason: Neo4j 5.26 has no query language accessor on the snapshot, so the field is never written on the LTS line; DozerDB invents no value for a field a line cannot supply.

fields.notes: CypherVersion.description from QuerySnapshot.queryLanguage(). The record's queryLanguage is null on a line without the accessor, and a null field is absent from the JSON. Absent from an early start entry (early_raw_logging_enabled) too: Neo4j settles the language in the pre-parse step, after the event that writes it (start-verbose-early).

fields.name: transaction.event

calendar.reason: No plain-text transaction entry is documented; DozerDB writes 'Transaction started: ', 'Transaction committed: ' or 'Transaction rolled back: ' before the entry. JSON names the event as documented.

lts.reason: No plain-text transaction entry is documented; DozerDB writes 'Transaction started: ', 'Transaction committed: ' or 'Transaction rolled back: ' before the entry. JSON names the event as documented.

fields.notes: JSON names the event as the manual documents it: start, commit or rollback. The plain marker is DozerDB's, since no plain-text transaction entry is documented. Every kernel transaction the monitor reports is a candidate, the system database's and Neo4j's own internal ones included, when db.logs.query.transaction.enabled selects it; a start entry needs VERBOSE, an end entry INFO with the open time at least db.logs.query.transaction.threshold, a rollback with a throwable always.

fields.name: transaction.transactionId

calendar.reason: The transaction's sequence number, the same number the query entries run inside it carry.

lts.reason: The transaction's sequence number, the same number the query entries run inside it carry.

fields.notes: KernelTransaction.getTransactionSequenceNumber(), the number the query entries run inside the transaction carry as their transaction id and SHOW TRANSACTIONS exposes; readable at start, commit and rollback.

fields.name: transaction.openTimeMs

calendar.reason: Plain text only, DozerDB's shape: how long the transaction had been open, measured at commit or rollback (0 at start), the figure db.logs.query.transaction.threshold filters on.

lts.reason: Plain text only, DozerDB's shape: how long the transaction had been open, measured at commit or rollback (0 at start), the figure db.logs.query.transaction.threshold filters on.

fields.notes: Measured by the adapter from the kernel transaction's own start clock (startTimeNanos) to the commit or rollback event, in whole milliseconds; 0 on a start entry. The kernel exposes no end time for a rollback, hence the measurement at the event.

fields.name: transaction.source

calendar.reason: Plain text only, DozerDB's shape: the transaction's connection details, as in a query entry; the manual lists no source for transaction entries.

lts.reason: Plain text only, DozerDB's shape: the transaction's connection details, as in a query entry; the manual lists no source for transaction entries.

fields.notes: KernelTransaction.clientInfo().asConnectionDetails(), the same connection details as a query entry's source (deprecated upstream; watchlist); embedded-session for Neo4j's internal transactions.

fields.name: transaction.database

calendar.reason: JSON as documented; in plain text after the source's tab, DozerDB's placement.

lts.reason: JSON as documented; in plain text after the source's tab, DozerDB's placement.

fields.notes: KernelTransaction.getDatabaseName(); never <none>, a kernel transaction always belongs to a database.

fields.name: transaction.executingUser

calendar.reason: JSON as documented; in plain text after the database, DozerDB's placement.

lts.reason: JSON as documented; in plain text after the database, DozerDB's placement.

fields.notes: KernelTransaction.securityContext().subject().executingUser(), which Neo4j keeps readable while the monitor runs at commit and rollback; empty with authentication disabled.

fields.name: transaction.authenticatedUser

calendar.reason: JSON only, as the manual lists it: the authenticated user of the transaction beside executingUser; the plain line shows the executing user alone.

lts.reason: JSON only, as the manual lists it: the authenticated user of the transaction beside executingUser; the plain line shows the executing user alone.

fields.notes: KernelTransaction.securityContext().subject().authenticatedUser(); differs from the executing user under impersonation. JSON only, always present when Neo4j supplies it, as on a query entry.

fields.name: transaction.annotationData

calendar.reason: Plain text only, DozerDB's shape: the transaction's metadata as a sorted-key Cypher map; the manual lists no annotation data for transaction entries.

lts.reason: Plain text only, DozerDB's shape: the transaction's metadata as a sorted-key Cypher map; the manual lists no annotation data for transaction entries.

fields.notes: KernelTransaction.getMetaData() read at the event: empty on a start entry (clients attach their metadata after the kernel reports the start) and the transaction's final metadata on a commit or rollback entry. Plain text only; the manual lists no annotation data for a transaction entry, so the JSON stays within the documented keys.

fields.name: transaction.failureReason

calendar.reason: DozerDB's shape in both layouts: a rollback with a throwable is written whatever the threshold, at ERROR as a failed-query entry is, because Neo4j's structured log carries a throwable at that level only; the plain line appends ' - <reason>' with the stack trace after, and the JSON entry carries the reason under failureReason, the key a failed-query entry uses, beside the layout's stacktrace. The manual lists no reason key for a transaction entry.

lts.reason: DozerDB's shape in both layouts: a rollback with a throwable is written whatever the threshold, at ERROR as a failed-query entry is, because Neo4j's structured log carries a throwable at that level only; the plain line appends ' - <reason>' with the stack trace after, and the JSON entry carries the reason under failureReason, the key a failed-query entry uses, beside the layout's stacktrace. The manual lists no reason key for a transaction entry.

fields.notes: The message of the throwable Neo4j hands the monitor's rollback event (a transaction event listener that refused the commit, for instance); null for a rollback the client asked for, and then no segment and no key. The throwable itself goes to Log4j, so the stack trace follows the plain line and is the JSON stacktrace field. The JSON key is failureReason, as on a failed-query entry, so a parser keyed on it finds failed transactions too (maintainer decision 2026-11-06); the other transaction keys stay exactly the manual's.

shapes.title: Start entry
shapes.text: Written at the VERBOSE detail level only, once the query is parsed and obfuscated. The manual's only start entry is a Neo4j 4.4 capture, so the current shape is DozerDB's: the end entry's grammar behind the documented `Query started: ` prefix, the timing, allocation and page figures at 0, `runtime=null`, and the annotation data the transaction carries so far. In JSON the entry has `event` `start`, no `runtime` key and the cache key hash `00000000`, as the manual documents for a start event.

shapes.title: Early start entry
shapes.text: With `db.logs.query.early_raw_logging_enabled=true` the start entry is written when the query is received, before parsing and obfuscation, so a query that hangs or fails in parsing is still recorded. It has one shape on every path, so a reader can tell it from a start entry written after planning: `transaction id:0` and the database `<none>`, because the query has reached neither yet (the end entry carries both); the raw query text and parameters (a literal stays visible under `obfuscate_literals`, a password literal is in clear; `parameter_logging_enabled` and `max_parameter_length` still apply); the figures at 0, `runtime=null`, the cache key hash `00000000` and, in JSON, no `queryLang`. A query has exactly one start entry, this one or the parsed one.

shapes.title: Failed-query entry
shapes.text: The manual documents no plain-text line for a failed query. DozerDB writes the entry at the Log4j level `ERROR` (every other entry is `INFO`): the success entry's line, then ` - ` and the failure reason Neo4j reported, which keeps its own line breaks (a syntax error adds the query and a caret), and the exception's stack trace on the lines after. In JSON the entry has `event` `fail`, the deprecated `failureReason` beside the documented `errorInfo` tree, because parsers key on either, and the layout's `stacktrace`. A failed query is logged at `INFO` whatever `db.logs.query.threshold` says, without the `id:` prefix, as at `VERBOSE` with it. A failure Neo4j reports without a reason ends with the annotation data.

shapes.title: Failed-query entry under `db.logs.query.obfuscate_errors`
shapes.text: Neo4j's obfuscated status description replaces the failure reason, and no stack trace follows the line, in either layout; in JSON `failureReason` and every `statusDescription` of `errorInfo` carry the obfuscated description and there is no `stacktrace`. A failure Neo4j reports without a GQL status object then carries no reason at all. On Neo4j 5.26, which has no obfuscated status description, the standard description of the GQLSTATUS code (its condition and sub-condition, without the message) stands in wherever the obfuscated one would.

shapes.title: A query never bound to a database
shapes.text: A query that failed before it was routed to a database (a parse error, for instance) has no database. The manual documents `<none>` for the JSON `database` field; DozerDB writes `<none>` in the plain line too, with `transaction id:-1`, Neo4j's own value for a query that never reached a transaction, and `runtime=null`, so nothing that reached the server is missing from the log.

shapes.title: Error without a GQL status on Neo4j 5.26
lines:
{"time":"2026-11-06 18:02:12.138+0000","level":"ERROR","allocatedBytes":0,"annotationData":"{}","authenticatedUser":"neo4j","database":"<none>","elapsedTimeMs":6,"errorInfo":{"GQLSTATUS":"50N42","statusDescription":"error: general processing exception - unexpected error. Unexpected error has occurred. See debug log for details."},"event":"fail","executingUser":"neo4j","executionPlanCacheKeyHash":"00000000","failureReason":"Variable `m` not defined (line 1, column 18 (offset: 17))
"MATCH (n) RETURN m"
                  ^","id":"5","pageFaults":0,"pageHits":0,"planning":6,"query":"MATCH (n) RETURN m","queryParameters":"{}","source":"bolt-session	bolt	neo4j-javascript/6.0.1		client/127.0.0.1:53864	server/127.0.0.1:7687>","transactionId":-1,"type":"query","waiting":0,"stacktrace":"org.neo4j.exceptions.SyntaxException: Variable `m` not defined (line 1, column 18 (offset: 17))
…"}
shapes.text: On Neo4j 5.26 some errors have no GQL status of their own: "variable not defined" is raised by the router before the query reaches a database. DozerDB writes what Neo4j 5.26 reports, so the failed-query entry's `errorInfo` carries the default `50N42` with no `position` and no `cause`, and its `database` is `<none>`, where the manual's example for the same query shows `42N62` with a position. An error that has a GQL status (an unaliased `WITH` item, for instance) carries its tree with the position at every level, as on the calendar line. The line below is the JSON entry Neo4j 5.26 gives for `MATCH (n) RETURN m`, its stack trace shortened here to the first line.

shapes.title: Source segment of HTTP and embedded queries
shapes.text: The source is Neo4j Community's own connection details, the same text Neo4j writes for a Bolt connection in the manual's examples (`bolt-session`, the protocol, the driver name and version, the client and server addresses, each after a tab). The manual shows no current example for the other sources: a query over the transactional endpoint (`POST /db/{database}/tx/commit`) is `server-session`, the scheme, the client host and the request path, each after a tab; a query over the Query API (`POST /db/{database}/query/v2`), which Neo4j serves over an in-process Bolt channel, is the Bolt shape with `neo4j-query-api/v2` as the client and the channel's local addresses (`clientlocal:...`, `serverlocal:...`), so the request path is not in the entry; an embedded query (Neo4j's own and a procedure's inner queries) is `embedded-session` followed by its own tab, so two tabs precede the database. Transaction entries carry the same segment.

shapes.title: Parameters: the cut value and the dropped segment
shapes.text: The manual's examples show `{}` only. DozerDB writes the parameters as Neo4j's single-line Cypher map (`{name: 'Alexander', n: 42}`, strings in single quotes, `{}` when there are none). `db.logs.query.max_parameter_length` cuts each value to that many characters and appends `...` inside the value, a string keeping its closing quote, so the entry still reads as a map (the first line, at a maximum of 10). `db.logs.query.parameter_logging_enabled=false` drops the segment and its ` - ` separator rather than writing `{}`, and the JSON key `queryParameters` is absent (the second line). A parameter value is never obfuscated by `db.logs.query.obfuscate_literals`, except that a password parameter is `'******'` at every setting.

shapes.title: Plan table
shapes.text: The manual says `queryPlan` is included under `db.logs.query.plan_description_enabled` and names the plan description table, but fixes neither its placement in the plain line nor its JSON type. DozerDB attaches the text Neo4j's `EXPLAIN` shows (the `Cypher`, `Planner`, `Runtime` and `Runtime version` header lines, the operator table, `Total database accesses: ?`) on the lines after the entry in plain text, and as one JSON string with the line breaks escaped, so the entry stays one object per line (the layout cuts any string over its maximum, 32 KiB with the shipped `neo4j.conf`). Only an end entry of a query that compiled carries it; a failed query that compiled has its table before its stack trace; a `PROFILE` query still gets the `EXPLAIN` shape, never profile figures.

shapes.title: `cpu` only when Neo4j tracks it
shapes.text: The JSON field `cpu` is present only while `db.track_query_cpu_time=true` (a dynamic setting): Neo4j's query snapshot has no CPU figure otherwise, and DozerDB never invents one. It never appears in the plain line, whose grammar is the same with or without it (the line below was written with the setting on).

shapes.title: Transaction entries
shapes.text: The manual documents transaction entries for the JSON layout only (`type` `transaction`, `event` `start`, `commit` or `rollback`, `transactionId`, `database`, `executingUser`, `authenticatedUser`), and DozerDB's JSON entry carries exactly those keys, plus `failureReason` on a rollback caused by a failure (the shape below). The plain-text line is DozerDB's: `Transaction started: `, `Transaction committed: ` or `Transaction rolled back: `, then `transaction id:N - N ms - <source>`, a tab, `<database> - <user> - <annotation data>`. The milliseconds are how long the transaction had been open at its commit or rollback (0 on a start entry), the figure `db.logs.query.transaction.threshold` selects on; the transaction id is the number the query entries run inside the transaction carry, so the two kinds of entry join on it; the annotation data is `{}` on a start entry, because clients attach their metadata after the kernel reports the start, and the final metadata on an end entry. Every kernel transaction is a candidate, the system database's and Neo4j's internal ones included; a rollback the client asked for carries no reason and stays at `INFO`.

shapes.title: Rollback caused by a failure
shapes.text: A rollback Neo4j reports with an exception (a transaction event listener that refused the commit, a constraint violation at commit) is written whatever the threshold, at the Log4j level `ERROR` like a failed-query entry, with ` - ` and the exception's message last and its stack trace on the lines after. In JSON the entry carries the manual's keys for a transaction entry, the exception's message under `failureReason` (the key a failed-query entry uses, which the manual does not list for a transaction entry) and the layout's `stacktrace`.

shapes.title: Fallback entry
lines: Query log entry could not be written: id:34 - java.lang.IllegalStateException: renderer broke
Query log entry could not be written: transaction id:12 - java.lang.IllegalStateException: renderer broke
shapes.text: An entry that cannot be rendered or written never fails the query or the transaction and never switches the log off; DozerDB writes a fallback entry in its place, at the Log4j level `ERROR`, naming the query id (or the transaction id) and the exception, so the gap is visible in `query.log` itself and not only in `debug.log`, where each kind of failure is reported once. In JSON the fallback is a `query` entry with the `id` and this text as its `failureReason`, or a `transaction` entry with the `transactionId`. Neo4j Enterprise has no counterpart; the shape is DozerDB's.
